dialogue.content: (こんばんは　本日はよろしくお願いいたします　お時間になりましたら開始させていただきます）
dialogue.English: (Good evening. Thank you for coming today. We will begin at the scheduled time.)

dialogue.content: よろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: こんばんは相談員ですここではどんなことでも安心しておはなしくださいね最初に年齢、性別、相談したい内容を教えてください
dialogue.English: Good evening, I'm the counselor. Please feel free to talk about anything here; you're in a safe space. To start, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you would like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いします。44歳、女性です。今日は子供のことで相談に来ました。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I'm a 44-year-old woman. I'm here today to talk about my child.

dialogue.content: 教えていただきありがとうございます子供のことについてということですが、詳細を教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that. You mentioned it's about your child. Could you please tell me more details?

dialogue.content: 小学生で塾に通ってますが仲良くない子がいるみたいで、時々嫌味を行ってくるから楽しくないの言います。
dialogue.English: My child is in elementary school and attends a cram school, but it seems there's another child they don't get along with. My child says it isn't fun because they sometimes make snide remarks.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね仲良くない子から嫌味を言ってくるのは、どれくらい前からなんですか？
dialogue.English: I see. How long has this child been making snide remarks to him?

dialogue.content: まだ塾が2ヶ月くらいなのですが、学校の違う子もいるので違う学校の子がからかう感じで言ってくるみたいです。
dialogue.English: He's only been at the cram school for about two months. There are children from other schools there, and it seems a child from a different school is teasing him.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですねお子様と一緒に過ごせない時に、そういったことがあるとなおさら心配になりますよね・・
dialogue.English: I understand. It must be especially worrying when things like that happen when you can't be with your child...

dialogue.content: 勉強を楽しくできるようになればいいと思ってクラス制の塾に行き始めたのですが、そもそも仲間が楽しくないのは困ったなと思っています。話を聞いて判断しか出来ないので…
dialogue.English: I had hoped he would start to enjoy studying, so he began attending a class-based cram school, but it's troubling that he's not enjoying the company there. All I can do is listen to him and try to figure things out...

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね今の塾がお母様がお子様にとってふさわしい場と判断されて入ったんですね
dialogue.English: I see. So you decided on this current cram school, believing it would be a suitable place for your child.

dialogue.content: 嫌味とは例えばどんなことがありましたか？
dialogue.English: For example, what kind of snide remarks were they?

dialogue.content: 友達と勉強すると楽しいかなと思ったのでいれました。うちの子はおそらくからかわれやすいタイプなのだと思います。勉強出来る訳でもないですし。身体が大きいのでそこをからかわれたりするようです。ただ素直に育ってくれているので強気に言い返すとかも出来ずに我慢してると思います。
dialogue.English: I enrolled him thinking it would be fun for him to study with friends. I think my son is probably the type who gets teased easily. He's not particularly good at his studies, either. He's big for his age, and it seems they tease him about that. But he has grown up to be a very gentle boy, so I think he just endures it without being able to talk back assertively.

dialogue.content: そうっだったんですねからかわれやすいタイプと思われるのは、以前もにたようなことがあったのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. When you say you think he's the type who gets teased easily, has something similar happened before?

dialogue.content: 何となくそう思います。
dialogue.English: I just have that feeling.

dialogue.content: そう思われるのですねどんなことに心当たりがありますか？
dialogue.English: You have that feeling. Is there anything specific that comes to mind?

dialogue.content: いじられやすそうなキャラといいますか…少し同学年の中では幼い考えの方と思います。
dialogue.English: He has a personality that's easy to pick on, I guess... I think his way of thinking is a bit immature for his age group.

dialogue.content: 少しぽっちゃり体型でもあります。
dialogue.English: He's also a bit on the chubby side.

dialogue.content: ちなみに息子様でしょうか？学年は何年生でしょうか？
dialogue.English: By the way, is it your son? What grade is he in?

dialogue.content: 6年生の男の子です。
dialogue.English: He's a sixth-grade boy.

dialogue.content: もう6年生なので、なるべくトラブルは自分で解決してくれたらいいなと思います。もちろん話は都度聞いてサポートはしたいと思います。
dialogue.English: Since he's already in the 6th grade, I hope he can resolve these troubles on his own as much as possible. Of course, I want to listen to him each time and provide support.

dialogue.content: 息子様を見守っていきたいという風にも思われてるんですね
dialogue.English: So you also feel that you want to watch over your son and let him handle it.

dialogue.content: 今回は息子様に対して特にどういった思いがつよいですか？
dialogue.English: In this situation, what are your strongest feelings or wishes regarding your son?

dialogue.content: そうですね。親が出ていくのがいいとも限りませんし、自分で解決して欲しいなと思います。例えば、先生に相談してみるとか自分から行動させてみようかなと思ってます
dialogue.English: That's right. It's not always best for a parent to intervene, so I'd like him to resolve it himself. For example, I'm thinking of encouraging him to take action on his own, like talking to his teacher.

dialogue.content: そう思われたんですね先生に相談をしてみるように行動させるのは、これからでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see that's what you're thinking. Is having him talk to the teacher something you plan to do from now on?

dialogue.content: はい。昨日子供からこの話を聞いたばかりなのでまだ何も。
dialogue.English: Yes. I just heard about this from my child yesterday, so we haven't done anything yet.

dialogue.content: 昨日のできごとだったんですねお話を聞いた時はどうお感じになりましたか？
dialogue.English: So you just heard about this yesterday. How did you feel when you heard his story?

dialogue.content: 2ヶ月前から塾に行ってますがいつから言われてるのかはハッキリ覚えてないみたいです。ずっと言われていたみたいです。気づくことは出来なかったから言ってくれてよかったと思いました。
dialogue.English: He's been attending the cram school for two months, but he doesn't clearly remember when it started. It seems it's been going on the whole time. I wasn't able to notice, so I was glad he told me.

dialogue.content: そうですよねお子様としては勇気を出してお話ししてくれたのかもしれないですね
dialogue.English: That's true. It might have taken a lot of courage for your child to talk to you about it.

dialogue.content: ハッキリいじめられてる訳では無いから、何となくモヤモヤがあってその子達がいると嫌だなと思って距離をとるみたいです。
dialogue.English: It's not that he's being clearly bullied; it's more of a vague discomfort. When those kids are around, he feels uncomfortable and seems to keep his distance.

dialogue.content: お子様自信でも対策をされているのですねしっかりしているお子様だと感じました
dialogue.English: So your son is taking measures on his own. He sounds like a very mature child.

dialogue.content: お母様としては今回でどのようになっていければとお考えでしょうか？
dialogue.English: As his mother, what kind of outcome are you hoping for in this situation?

dialogue.content: まずは解決するキッカケを作りたいと思っています
dialogue.English: First, I'd like to create an opportunity to resolve it.

dialogue.content: そうですよね具体的には先ほどお話しされた、先生に相談させるというようなことでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. Specifically, do you mean what you mentioned earlier—having him consult the teacher?

dialogue.content: そうなんです。子供同士で話すだけだとトラブルになる可能性もあるので、やはり塾の先生に1度相談するべきかなと思っているのです。
dialogue.English: That's right. Just having the children talk among themselves could lead to more trouble, so I think he should probably consult with the cram school teacher at least once.

dialogue.content: 冷静にご判断をされたんですね賢明なご判断だと思います
dialogue.English: You've made a very calm and collected decision. I think it's a wise judgment.

dialogue.content: 自分で言ってみるのは勇気が必要かもですが、まずはやってみるからかなと思います。
dialogue.English: It might take courage for him to say it himself, but I think the first step is for him to try.

dialogue.content: そうですよね行動に移せることがお子様にとっても大きな成長になると私も思います
dialogue.English: Yes. I also believe that taking action will be a significant step in his growth.

dialogue.content: お子様は先生に言えそうだと思いますか？
dialogue.English: Do you think your son will be able to talk to the teacher?

dialogue.content: まだちゃんと伝えてないのでわからないです。
dialogue.English: I haven't properly suggested it to him yet, so I don't know.

dialogue.content: 一人っ子なのでこういったトラブルもはじめてですし、私自身も親としてどうしたら正解なのかが分からなくて子供と対策は話せてないです。
dialogue.English: He's an only child, so this is the first time we've had this kind of trouble. As a parent, I myself don't know the right thing to do, so I haven't been able to discuss countermeasures with him yet.

dialogue.content: 初めてだと何が正解か不安な気持ちになりますよねそんな中あなたは確実に行動できていて素晴らしいと感じました
dialogue.English: It's natural to feel anxious about what the right answer is when it's the first time. In the midst of that, I feel it's wonderful that you are taking concrete steps to address this.

dialogue.content: どういった感じでお子様に伝える予定ですか？
dialogue.English: How do you plan to bring this up with your son?

dialogue.content: まずは自分で解決してみるのはどうかな？って気持ちを聞きたいと思います。
dialogue.English: First, I want to ask for his thoughts on it, something like, 'What do you think about trying to resolve this yourself?'

dialogue.content: いけそうなら先生に相談してみたら？と言おうかなと。
dialogue.English: If he seems up for it, I'm thinking of suggesting, "How about talking to your teacher?"

dialogue.content: ええ、お子様の気持ちもしっかり尊重されてるのですね
dialogue.English: Yes, you're clearly respecting your child's feelings.

dialogue.content: いけない場合はどうしますか？
dialogue.English: What will you do if he doesn't feel up to it?

dialogue.content: 友達とのトラブルは私も経験ありますから、いけない場合は無理させず一緒に言いに塾に行こうと思います。
dialogue.English: I've also experienced troubles with friends, so if he can't do it, I won't force him. I'll go to the cram school with him to talk to them.

dialogue.content: お母様の方で直接お話しされるのですね無理をさせないという判断は素晴らしいと思います
dialogue.English: So you would talk to them directly yourself. I think your decision not to force him is wonderful.

dialogue.content: 今まで学校はトラブルなく楽しく行ってたので、塾でのトラブルだから私も責任感じてはいるのです。
dialogue.English: He's always had fun at his regular school without any trouble, so because this is a problem at the cram school, I feel a sense of responsibility.

dialogue.content: そう感じているのですね塾の環境の影響でもありますので、必ずしもあなたの責任だけではないと思います
dialogue.English: I understand that's how you feel. The cram school environment also plays a role, so I don't think it's solely your responsibility.

dialogue.content: もしお子様が自分で行けそうだと判断された場合ぜひ勇気づけの言葉をかけて上げれたらと思います
dialogue.English: If he decides he can go on his own, I hope you can offer him some words of encouragement.

dialogue.content: 楽しく勉強のために行かせたのにトラブルなんて、可哀想なことしたなとおもってます。
dialogue.English: I sent him there so he could enjoy studying, and yet he's having trouble—I feel sorry for putting him through that.

dialogue.content: 勇気づけの言葉はどんなのがいいでしょう？
dialogue.English: What kind of encouraging words would be good?

dialogue.content: そのようにお感じなのですね
dialogue.English: I see that's how you're feeling.

dialogue.content: はい、例えば○○（お子様の名前）、お母さんはあなたの味方だからねきっと○○なら、乗り越えられるよ自分を信じてやってみて
dialogue.English: Yes, for example: "[Son's Name], Mom is always on your side. I'm sure you can get through this. Believe in yourself and give it a try."

dialogue.content: お母さんは味方だからって素敵な言葉ですね！使ってみます！ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: "Mom is on your side" is a wonderful thing to say! I'll try using it! Thank you.

dialogue.content: お母様の方で一言勇気づけれると、背中を押してもらえたと感じてくれると思いますよ
dialogue.English: If you offer just one word of encouragement, I think he'll feel like you've given him a supportive push.

dialogue.content: ええ、ぜひ使ってみてくださいね
dialogue.English: Yes, please do try it.

dialogue.content: はい！
dialogue.English: I will!

dialogue.content: 本日は素敵なお話を聞かせてくれてありがとうございますお時間がそろそろとなってまいりました
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing your story with me today. Our time is almost up.

dialogue.content: 昨日から1人で考えていたので話してみてよかったです。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: I've been thinking about this by myself since yesterday, so I'm glad I had the chance to talk about it. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: そう言ってもらえて私もうれしいです
dialogue.English: I'm happy to hear you say that.

dialogue.content: ぜひここでまた、どうなったかお話し聞かせてくださいね
dialogue.English: Please feel free to come back and let me know how things go.

dialogue.content: そうですね！ありがとうございます！
dialogue.English: Yes, I will! Thank you!

dialogue.content: それでは本日は以上とさせていただきます本日はありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Then we'll conclude for today. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: 失礼いたします
dialogue.English: Goodbye.

dialogue.content: 失礼します。
dialogue.English: Goodbye.

dialogue.content: （お疲れさまでした　本日はありがとうございましたお時間あるときに、ロールプレイの評価をお願いいたします）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for your efforts today. Thank you very much. When you have time, please provide an evaluation of the role-play.)

dialogue.content: （それでは終了させていただきます）
dialogue.English: (We will now end the session.)
